acceptanceCriteria.statement: Systems Max knows about match the characteristics already observed (type of star, known planets, etc.): arriving at a known real system spawns its real structure from the ingested data (exoplanet archive + curated companion table) via the overlay merge — NOT via new KnownSystems registry entries (findAt at Sirius stays null; authoring stays scoped to Alpha Centauri in AC5).

verifyVia.input: Warp to Sirius and to TRAPPIST-1 (any targeting path).
verifyVia.observable: Sirius: A-class primary plus its white-dwarf companion present as a binary, sourced from the curated companion table (companion class D per AC10 engine support). TRAPPIST-1: M-dwarf with its seven known planets carrying their real designations (b–h) and archive-derived parameters. Star class matches the sky/catalog on every arrival path.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When real data runs out, the system fills the rest with procgen (Elite as the guide): known planets appear per the ingested data, procgen deterministically completes the remainder; real star type always comes from the catalog; real structure (multiplicity) applies exactly where the companion table covers it (the table may also pin famous singles), and procgen fills structure elsewhere. ADOPTED 2026-07-13 (deviation to post-review ruling 6): an archive snum==1 on a non-table host is an implicit single-pin — a real host whose archive record says the system has exactly one star suppresses the procgen companion roll. One-directional (it only suppresses fabrication, never adds structure; snum>=2 hosts keep the live roll) and the curated table still wins wherever both apply.

verifyVia.input: Headless: generate contents twice for (a) a real system with partial known planets, (b) a real star with zero known planets and no companion-table entry, (c) a companion-table binary, (d) a pinned-single star, (e) a snum==1 non-table real host on a seed that would roll a binary, through the real arrival pipeline (StarSystemGenerator + overlay merge).
verifyVia.observable: (a) all known planets present with archive-derived parameters, remainder procgen-filled, both runs identical (deep-equal on systemData; revisit-stable); (b) catalog star type preserved, structure and planets fully procgen, identical across runs; (c) table-specified companion class present, identical across runs; (d) singleness honored — procgen may not invent a companion for a pinned single; (e) the snum==1 non-table host produces NO companion (isBinary false, star2 null) on a seed that WOULD roll a binary absent the pin, with any known planets intact and both runs identical — while a snum>=2 non-table host keeps its live roll (one-directional boundary) and a table-covered host ignores snum (curated table wins).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The engine can represent observed stellar structure (it currently cannot: star types stop at O/B/A/F/G/K/M and systemData carries at most star + star2): a degenerate/white-dwarf star class works end-to-end (generation contents + rendering parameters, no G-type fallback warning), the generation context gains overlay fields (companion spec, known-planet list), and a far-companion representation covers the Alpha Centauri family. Representation cap is explicit and documented: at most 2 close stars per system; wide companions are represented as far companions or adjacent real systems; closer higher-order multiples collapse to the brightest pair with a documented caveat.
